card.title: Senior Manager, Global Visual Merchandising Production
card.description:
**Michael Kors is always interested in hearing from talented, globally-minded individuals with a passion for fashion.**

**If you enjoy working in a creative, fast-paced environment, then we would love to hear from you!**

—

**Who You Are:**

The Senior Manager, Global Visual Merchandising Production will lead the strategic planning, creative execution, and global production of visual merchandising activations across the Michael Kors retail network. This role is responsible for delivering innovative, brand-elevating experiences that drive customer engagement while ensuring operational excellence, fiscal responsibility, and flawless execution worldwide.

 

Working closely with Global Visual Experience, Store Design, Marketing, Creative Services, Supply Chain, and regional partners, the Senior Manager will oversee the end-to-end production lifecycle for seasonal campaigns, retail environments, windows, in-store experiences, and new store openings. This role will also lead vendor strategy, production innovation, and team development to support the continued growth of the brand globally.

 

**What You’ll Do:**

**Strategic Leadership**

* Define and lead the global production strategy for all Visual Merchandising assets, while providing direct leadership and oversight for the North America region, ensuring alignment with brand, business, and market objectives.
* Own the performance and evolution of the global production function, including operating models, production capabilities, quality standards, vendor networks, and operational effectiveness.
* Establish scalable production processes, governance, and resource strategies that support current business priorities and future growth across North America, EMEA, and APAC.
* Serve as the strategic advisor to Visual Merchandising, Design, and Creative teams, influencing decisions related to feasibility, engineering, materials, fabrication, innovation, and investment priorities.
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives that enhance speed-to-market, scalability, sustainability, quality, and cost efficiency while maintaining brand integrity.
* Champion the adoption of AI-enabled tools and emerging technologies to streamline workflows, improve operational efficiency, enhance decision-making, and identify opportunities to simplify and modernize Visual Merchandising production process globally.

**Global Production Management**

* Lead the end-to-end production lifecycle for all global Visual Merchandising programs, including windows, props, visual tools, branded environments, animations, and special activations.
* Oversee planning, budgeting, fabrication, logistics, installation, and execution across retail, outlet, wholesale, and special project channels.
* Ensure all programs are delivered on time, within budget, and to the highest standards of quality, craftsmanship, and brand consistency.
* Drive cross-functional project management across multiple concurrent initiatives, balancing competing priorities, business needs, and market requirements.
* Proactively identify executional risks and develop mitigation plans to ensure successful delivery across regions and stakeholders.

**Financial & Vendor Management**

* Own global production budget planning, forecasting, capital investment recommendations, and overall financial performance.
* Develop cost optimization strategies and scalable sourcing models that improve efficiency without compromising quality, customer experience, or brand standards.
* Build and manage strategic partnerships with fabricators, printers, logistics providers, installation partners, and other key vendors worldwide.
* Establish vendor performance metrics, accountability measures, and continuous improvement initiatives to ensure best-in-class execution.
* Evaluate production investments, operating models, and resource requirements, providing recommendations based on business impact, risk, and return on investment.

**Executive Influence & Cross-Functional Leadership**

* Serve as the senior production partner to Visual Merchandising, Store Design, Marketing, Procurement, Finance, Supply Chain, and regional leadership teams.
* Influence decision-making through data-driven recommendations, business acumen, and a comprehensive understanding of brand, customer, operational, and financial priorities.
* Build alignment across functions and regions while balancing competing priorities to achieve the best overall business outcome.
* Represent the production function in senior leadership discussions, ensuring production considerations are incorporated into broader business planning.
* Lead organizational change initiatives and drive adoption of new processes, technologies, and ways of working that improve operational effectiveness globally.

**Team & Organizational Leadership**

* Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing production team while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.
* Build organizational capability by developing future leaders, strengthening succession plans, and creating scalable ways of working.
* Establish clear performance expectations, operating rhythms, and development plans that enable increasing levels of ownership and autonomy across the team.
* Allocate resources strategically to ensure effective execution across a complex portfolio of global initiatives.
Create an environment where proactive problem-solving, strategic thinking, and enterprise leadership are expected at all levels. 

 

**You’ll Need to Have:**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Visual Merchandising, Production Management, Design, Construction Management or a related field.
* PMP certification or equivalent project management credentials preferred.
* 7-10 years of progressive experience in visual production, retail marketing production, environmental design, experiential production, or related fields.
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing high-performing teams in a global environment.
* Proven success leading large-scale, multi-market production programs within a premium or luxury retail organization.
* Strong expertise in project management, fabrication, print production, logistics, and installation processes.
Experience managing multimillion-dollar budgets and complex vendor ecosystems. 

 

**We’d Love to See:**

* Exceptional leadership, communication, influencing, and stakeholder management skills.
* Strong strategic thinking with the ability to translate creative vision into operational execution.
* Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
* Expertise in vendor negotiations, contract management, and cost optimization.
* Strong analytical and financial acumen.
* Highly collaborative with experience working across global, matrixed organizations.
* Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite, project management platforms, and collaborative workplace tools.

**REYNOLDS AMERICAN has an exciting opportunity for a Supply Network & Manufacturing Contingency Design Senior Manager in Winston-Salem, NC**

What happens to supply when a critical manufacturing site suddenly becomes unavailable?

We're looking for a **Supply Network & Manufacturing Contingency Design Senior Manager** to help answer that question before a disruption happens.

You'll develop and maintain manufacturing contingency strategies that protect continuity of supply, volume, revenue and gross margin across a complex manufacturing network. You'll identify and qualify alternative production sites and ensure critical manufacturing locations have credible, executable recovery strategies.

**Your key responsibilities will include****:**

* Coordinate product transfers, trials and validation activities.

* Team:Industrial Operations & Product Supply
* Location:Saratoga Springs

* Work Pattern:Onsite

**The role**
------------

**Build our future together:**

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We’re hiring a Sr. Director/ Executive Director of Manufacturing Operations for our new highly automated bulk/ drug substance manufacturing plant, supporting 20–30 tech transfers a year alongside commercial delivery responsibility. GMP production will run concurrently with construction and CQV for 3–5 years. This role requires both building and operating.

 
 

This site operates on a foundation of strategy, execution, and rigor. Every function at the site owns a pyramid of metrics derived from annual goal planning that connects the site’s strategic goals to the factory floor, with performance measured back up to leadership to monitor, track, and mitigate against contingencies quantified using SMART goals in days and dollars.

 
 

The Sr. Director/ Executive Director of Manufacturing Operations owns cross-suite production performance across upstream and downstream operations in both single-use and stainless-steel suites. As the site scales to six suites, this leader is accountable for delivery of the site production plan, manufacturing cost performance, and workforce strategy, drives daily operational discipline through MDI and lean standard work, and represents manufacturing on the site Leadership Team.

 
 

**When & where:**

* Location: Saratoga Springs, New York, United States

* Work model: Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm
 

 

**Discover your role:**

* Own cross-suite production performance and site-wide annual batch plan attainment across all operating suites

* Lead fully integrated, operations-focused suite teams, with upstream, downstream, and support activities managed within each suite, and clear day-to-day accountability for execution, staffing, and scheduling

* Oversee these functions OpEx and CapEx budget and roadmap

* Serve as the primary responsible party for this function's alignment with the Global Center of Excellence (COE), connecting site execution back to the business-level function

* Ensure this function's metrics flow up and down through the MDI structure, connecting into the site's S&OP, AOP, and long-range planning cycles

* Champion adoption of lean principles across manufacturing including standardized work, visual controls, and a culture of continuous improvement (kaizen) as the site scales to six suites

* Lead the production plan across all suites, working with supply chain to align the supply plan to the production schedule through the site S&OP process

* Drive the site's daily MFG MDI process at the suite level surfacing, escalating, and resolving issues in real time across all shifts

* Serve as the manufacturing process and cost owner, driving cost-per-batch performance and contributing to the site Annual Operating Plan (AOP) and budget

* Manage workforce strategy and ramp for the manufacturing organization, including multi-shift staffing, hiring, training, and qualification of operators as new suites come online

* Ensure cGMP compliance, right-first-time execution, and inspection readiness on the manufacturing floor, partnering closely with Quality on deviations and batch record performance

* Champion a zero-harm EHS culture and drive manufacturing safety performance across all shifts

* Lead manufacturing operational readiness for suites entering service, partnering with Technical Services on tech transfer, process readiness, and PPQ execution

* Build and maintain a lean, scalable manufacturing organization, including area management and round-the-clock shift coverage within each suite

* Partner with quality, technical services, supply chain, environmental health & safety, and operational excellence to resolve issues quickly and operate as one aligned site leadership team

* Establish high standards for performance management and accountability; develop and retain talent; perform other duties as required

* Own a gross margin improvement program and goal for this function, contributing to the site's overall margin performance
 

 

**This role requires****:**

* B.S in engineering, life sciences, or a related technical field
 + Sr. Director: 15+ years in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, including large-molecule drug substance operations including 7+ years of progressive leadership
 + Executive Director: 18+ years in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, including large-molecule drug substance operations including 7+ years of progressive leadership
 + Level will be determined based on experience
* Financially literate, with demonstrated experience of delivering production plan attainment, managing cost per batch, and operating within an annual budget

* Experience leading the start-up and ramp of manufacturing suites or facilities

* Experience leading large, multi-shift GMP organizations and building leadership depth

* Previous people leadership/supervisory experience

At Westinghouse, we recognize that our employees are our most valuable asset and we seek to identify, attract and recruit the most qualified talent while recognizing and encouraging the value of diversity in the global workplace.

### **About the role:**

As a Senior Manager of MFG Engineering Programs in our New Product Introduction group, you will be responsible and accountable to lead and deliver global nuclear fuel manufacturing project execution across Westinghouse Electric Corporation (WEC) fuel manufacturing facilities in the US, UK & Sweden operations. You will be deployed to guide progress and execution of multiple projects within our organization, based on the program needs. The Sr Manager owns the global manufacturing scope of new product introduction and is accountable to lead project execution to delivery in-full, without complaint products to our customers while meeting safety and financial goals. This position will guide interaction between Fuel Engineering, Nuclear Fuel Project Managers, Product Delivery & Commercial Managers, Product Management, Supply Chain, SIOP, Plant Manufacturing Managers, Global Quality, and Supplier or customer teams. It will also coordinate on project deliverables, issues, and resolution. Program budget accountability ranges from $1M - $20M.

You will report to the Director of New Product Introduction and support the role remotely with 25 - 35% travel between global manufacturing facilities.

 

### **Key Responsibilities:**

* Comprehend entire program scope, such as commercial, licensing, regulatory and initiate appropriate scope within the manufacturing program scope.
* Support project task-based schedules and track/report milestone progress against the program management plan.
* Deploy strategies for optimizing and streamlining legacy fuel manufacturing operations in partnership with manufacturing sites and functional leads.
* Analyze existing processes and identify value-added and non-value-added activities to solve design challenges.
* Manage project risks and opportunities to closure in partnership with functional leads and Program Managers. Identify issues, propose solutions and lead recovery plans to closure.
* Implement within project schedule and budget, tracking expenses and identifying cost-savings opportunities. Communicate with partners, providing updates on project milestones, risks, critical escalations and issues.
* Present strategic project reports, status updates, and performance metrics to senior leadership and important partners.
* Identify areas of improvement or gaps in current processes and develop strategies to promote efficiency and productivity in new product and process introduction.
* Perform as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) to support project teams in new product and process development such as APQP and PPAP industry standards.
* Compare actual performance against planned performance to identify variances and help manage tasks on project planning.
* Collaborate with program team members and departments to establish plans and schedules that allocate resources to best achieve program requirements and service internal and external client or customer needs.

### **Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering or related field.
* 10 -15 years related experience in Nuclear/ Automotive/ Heavy Engineering/ Metals Industry / Manufacturing / Assembly.
* Experience with project management and new product introduction into manufacturing.
* Analytical capabilities to identify critical schedule paths and improve engineering / supply chain timelines.
* Demonstrated skills in internal operational partner relationship management.
* Advance level PMI certification in Project Management.
* Experience of Engineering Component Manufacturing systems.
* Experience with engineering product development including design phases, manufacturing processes and global supply chain management.
* Familiarization with Kaizen, Lean Operations, FMEA's, DMAIC, DFMAs, POCA cycles.
* Familiarization with Microsoft Project, P6 or other scheduling software.

 

We are committed to transparency and equity in all of our people practices. The base salary range for this position, which is dependent upon experience, qualifications and skills, is estimated to be $144,000 to $180,000 per year.

* Comprehensive Medical benefits which could include medical, dental, vision, prescription coverage and Health Savings Account (HSA) with employer contributions options
* Wellness Programs designed to support employees in maintaining their health and well-being including Employee Assistance Program providing support for our employees and their household members
* 401(k) with Company Match Contributions to support employees' retirement
* Paid Vacations and Company Holidays
* Opportunities for Flexible Work Arrangements to promote work-life balance
* Educational Reimbursement and Comprehensive Career Programs to help employees grow in their careers
* Global Recognition and Service Programs to celebrate employee accomplishments and service
* Employee Referral Program

* Safety and Quality
* Integrity and Trust
* Customer Focus and Innovation
* Speed and Passion to Win
* Teamwork and Accountability

 

**While our Global Headquarters are located in Cranberry Township, PA, we have over 11,000 employees working at locations in 19 different countries. You can learn more by visiting** http://www.westinghousenuclear.com.

 

Westinghouse is an Equal Opportunity Employer including Veterans and Individuals with Disabilities

### **Senior Manager, Operational Excellence - Factor US**

***This role is hybrid to our Goodyear, AZ Factor facility***

### **Company Overview**

At Factor, we are on a mission to revolutionize the way people eat by making healthy, fresh, chef-prepared meals accessible and effortless. As the market leader in the Ready-To-Eat (RTE) meal space, we eliminate the need for cooking and meal prep while delivering high-quality, nutrition-focused meals directly to millions of customers. The Factor team is diverse, high-performing, and fast-growing, offering an inspiring environment where process innovation, operational discipline, and continuous improvement thrive.

### **About the role**

The **Senior Manager, Operational Excellence** leads OpEx capability and multi-site improvement programs across Factor's US ready-to-eat fulfillment, production and distribution network. The role owns projects end to end, from charter and business case through delivery and post-mortem. It combines Lean and Six Sigma methods with senior project-management discipline.

You will serve as a lead advocate for operational transformation by partnering with and challenging business leaders to adopt systems thinking and continuous process innovation.

### **You will...**

* Lead strategic Factor operations projects in continuous improvement, change management, cost optimization and OpEx training across RTE fulfillment networks.
* Direct complex, cross-facility improvement programs, coordinating site leadership with central project teams.
* Own project governance end to end: find high-ROI opportunities, write financially justified charters and capital project justifications, negotiate resources, launch teams, track results and remove roadblocks.
* Deliver projects to demanding schedules and aggressive cost targets, often with changing requirements. Routinely assess project risks and identify alternative paths to offset them.
* Lead the cross-functional project prioritization workflow and scoping program, and facilitate the project pipeline for all stakeholders.
* Develop, improve and maintain the project management process for the organization, and ensure best practices are followed.
* Build organized project plans from complex inputs, track status across a large program, and keep accurate records through frequent iterations.
* Identify new technologies that can deliver meaningful benefits, and champion changes that drive measurable operational improvements.
* Oversee material handling equipment, automation and warehouse projects. Serve as liaison between vendors and site maintenance, operations and technology teams.
* Apply DMAIC, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping and 5-Why to eliminate root causes of operational friction.
* Lead change management and risk mitigation for key operational shifts.
* Capture and scale best practices across production and fulfillment sites.
* Mentor junior project managers, Lean practitioners and floor supervisors in complex system integrations, and provide leadership to assigned teams so key competencies are developed and maintained.
* Support COGS reporting and tool creation. Data-driven, sound bridges, and coordinate actions that reduce COGS.

### **You are...**

* **Strategic leadership:** Influences without direct authority and aligns multi-site leaders around shared operational goals.
* **Project and time management:** Delivers multi-phase process and infrastructure projects on time and within budget.
* **Organization:** Builds organized project plans from complex inputs and keeps accurate records across frequent iterations.
* **Enterprising and creative:** Starts new operational and strategic projects, and challenges conventional methods with new ideas.
* **Cross-functional collaboration**: Bridges Central Strategy, Food Safety & Quality Assurance, Logistics, Procurement and DC Operations.
* **Stakeholder facilitation:** Negotiates, facilitates and resolves conflicting priorities across local and central stakeholders.
* **Communication:** Independently manages the cadence of formal and informal communication across all levels of the organization.
* **Critical thinking:** Weighs the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions before committing.
* **Data-driven**: Interprets operational telemetry, unit economics and process-flow metrics to make decisions.
* **Coaching and mentorship:** Coaches floor supervisors, Lean practitioners and project managers with constructive, empathy-driven feedback.
* **Driven by results**: Pushes projects to completion with urgency, focused on tangible business outcomes.

### **You have...**

* Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain, or equivalent management experience.
* 7+ years of experience in continuous improvement / OpEx roles within food manufacturing, RTE operations, or cold-chain logistics.
* Has led cross-facility or multi-site improvement programs.
* Hands-on use of DMAIC, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping and 5-Why.
* Master Black Belt or PMP Certification preferred.
* Extensive experience with Google Workspace.
* Experience with project management software.
* Experience utilizing AI tools and workflows.

### **Travel...**

* Travel: 25%-50% across Factor's national US fulfillment and production network

### **You'll get...**

* Competitive salary, 401k with company match that vests immediately upon participation
* Generous PTO, including sabbatical, and parental leave of up to 16 weeks
* Comprehensive health and wellness benefits with options at $0 monthly, effective first day of employment
* Tuition reimbursement for continuing education (upon 2 years of service)
* Up to 85% discount on subscriptions to HelloFresh meal plans (HelloFresh, Green Chef, Everyplate, and Factor\_)
* Access to Employee Resource Groups that are open to all employees, including those pertaining to BIPOC, women, veterans, parents, and LGBTQ+
* Inclusive, collaborative, and dynamic work environment within a fast-paced, mission-driven company that is disrupting the traditional food supply chain

This job description is intended to provide a general overview of the responsibilities. However, the Company reserves the right to adjust, modify, or reassign work tasks and responsibilities as needed to meet changing business needs, operational requirements, or other factors.

card.title: Sr. Director, Additive Manufacturing Systems Engineering
card.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.




WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

Hadrian is building an additive manufacturing capability that runs as part of an autonomous factory, not as a room full of printers. The hard problem is not any single machine, material, or line of code. It is making all of them behave as one system. Systems engineering is the glue that holds that system together, and this role owns the glue.

The Senior Director leads three engineering functions, materials and process engineering, hardware engineering, and software engineering, and is accountable for the digital backbone that binds them to each other and to applications engineering: the architecture, interfaces, and data that connect Hadrian’s Opus platform to cutting-edge additive manufacturing equipment, add automation where it makes sense, fuse sensor data into the part record, and turn a collection of parts into a full, integrated digital manufacturing system built around additive.

The measure of success is not three strong teams. It is one manufacturing system that a customer part flows through, from design intent to qualified hardware, with every decision and every data point captured along the way.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Architect the system. Define and control the end-to-end architecture for additive at Hadrian: requirements, interfaces, data model, and acceptance criteria that hold across multiple equipment platforms, modalities, and sites. Treat the factory as the product.

 - Build the digital backbone. Connect additive equipment, peripherals, and inspection assets to Opus with the same discipline a semiconductor fab applies to connecting tools to the host: standardized state models, telemetry, event streams, and data contracts, with security and configuration control built in.

 - Fuse the sensors. Bring in-situ monitoring, machine telemetry, environmental data, and downstream inspection into one correlated record per part, then move from monitoring to data-driven release and, where it is justified, closed-loop control.

 - Automate where it pays. Lead automation across additive cells (material and powder handling, build changeover, part removal and depowdering, post-processing flow, robotics, controls, and safety) with a written case for each: safety, repeatability, and data capture first; labor second. Never automate an unstable process.

 - Lead the three functions as one. Set standards, priorities, and cadence for materials and process, hardware, and software engineering. Resolve conflicts between them at the architecture level, not the escalation level.

 - Own the applications engineering interface. With the Head of Applications Engineering, define what a production-ready hand-off looks like, publish the process capability and design-rule data applications engineers build to, and close the loop from floor results back into design guidance.

 - Industrialize the equipment. Through the hardware engineering leader, own factory and site acceptance, commissioning, reliability (preventive maintenance, spares, MTBF/MTTR), and configuration-controlled modification and upgrade of additive systems, and lead the technical relationships with equipment partners that unlock deeper integration. The machine-level depth lives in that team; the standards and the outcomes live here.

 - Design for the factory. Partner with Factory Development and Factory Automation on cell and site design: material flow, capacity, simulation, utilities, and the path to lights-out operation for additive.

 - Build quality in. Make the system itself the evidence: traceability, data integrity, and process control that stand up to AS9100 audits and customer qualification without a separate paper trail.

 - Be the additive voice in Hadrian’s platform. Carry additive requirements into Core Engineering and the Opus roadmap, and bring platform capability back to the floor.

 - Hire, develop, and retain. Build a leadership bench under you, set a high technical bar, and make Hadrian the place the best additive systems engineers in the country want to work.
 


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a physical science; an advanced degree is strongly preferred.

 - 12+ years in advanced manufacturing, with real depth in at least three of these six domains: factory design and industrial automation; semiconductor or other high-reliability capital-equipment engineering; manufacturing software and data systems; materials science and process engineering; quality systems in regulated industries; sensing, process monitoring, and sensor fusion.

 - 5+ years leading engineering teams, including leading through managers and building at least one function from the ground up.

 - Production experience with metal laser powder bed fusion, as a user of the equipment, a developer of it, or both.

 - Has led the integration of complex equipment into factory-level software (manufacturing execution, equipment host, or data platforms), including requirements, interface standards, and acceptance criteria.

 - Has taken at least one production automation or capital-equipment program (robotic cells, material handling, or equipment with safety systems and controls) from concept through commissioning in a regulated environment (aerospace and defense, semiconductor, medical, or similar), and has owned the reliability of production equipment afterward.

 - Fluent across the stack: can review a process flow, a data schema, a metallurgical cross-section, and a controls narrative in the same meeting, and knows which one is lying.

 - Has worked as a true peer to a customer-facing or design function, with a record of building clean interfaces rather than absorbing the other team.

 - Willing to travel up to 20%, including to Hadrian sites and international partners. Must meet the ITAR requirements below.
 


WHAT WILL SET YOU APART

 - Ph.D. in materials science, mechanical engineering, systems engineering or a related discipline.

 - Semiconductor capital-equipment background: equipment-to-host integration, tool matching, fleet data, fault detection and statistical process control at scale.

 - Equipment-maker experience developing or launching metal additive systems (new product introduction, cost-productivity trades, design reviews) in addition to user-side experience.

 - In-situ monitoring and sensor fusion implemented in production, with data-driven release or closed-loop control.

 - Factory design: material flow planning, discrete-event simulation, and highly automated or lights-out operations.

 - AS9100 and customer qualification pathways; familiarity with AM specifications (ASTM F42, ISO/ASTM 529xx, SAE AMS 7xxx series).

 - Budget or P&L ownership of a capital-intensive program, with a record of making the build-versus-buy and automate-versus-wait calls well.

 - Modern software fluency: APIs, event streaming, OT/IT architecture, industrial interoperability standards (OPC UA, MTConnect), and cloud data platforms.

card.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 



Job Description

We are seeking a highly motivated engineer to support the design, development, integration, and fielding of a next-generation autonomous aircraft system. This position requires a balance of technical rigor, rapid decision-making, and hands-on engineering to efficiently transition concepts into operational capability. The ideal candidate is comfortable solving complex problems, taking ownership, working within an accelerated aircraft development environment, and is motivated by getting meaningful capability into the hands of operators quickly.

This role sits within the Manufacturing Programs organization and focuses on the front end of new aircraft and defense programs. The Staff Engineer, Advanced Manufacturing Programs will lead manufacturing strategy and planning for proposals, capture efforts, internal investment decisions, and early program development. You will work across Product Development, Manufacturing Engineering, Production, Supply Chain, Quality, Test, Facilities, Finance, and Program Management to translate aircraft concepts and program requirements into credible industrial plans. This role requires the technical depth to challenge assumptions, build defensible cost and schedule inputs, and carry manufacturing commitments from proposal through program execution.



What You’ll Do

 - Lead the manufacturing workstream for defense proposals, capture efforts, and strategic planning activities, from initial concept through final submission and customer follow-up.

 - Translate aircraft architecture, design maturity, delivery requirements, production rates, and schedule constraints into executable manufacturing and industrialization concepts.

 - Develop defensible bases of estimate for recurring labor, non-recurring engineering, headcount, tooling, equipment, facilities, production support, and manufacturing schedule inputs.

 - Build production rate, capacity, staffing, learning-curve, and ramp models; develop conceptual factory flows, station strategies, resource loading, and major milestone plans.

 - Lead rapid trade studies covering make-versus-buy decisions, vertical integration, manufacturing processes, automation, tooling strategy, factory footprint, capital investment, and surge capacity.

 - Integrate inputs from Product Development, Manufacturing Engineering, Production, Supply Chain, MP&L, Quality, Test, Facilities, Finance, and Program Management into one coherent manufacturing approach.

 - Author clear customer-facing proposal content, manufacturing plans, cost and schedule narratives, risk and opportunity assessments, and responses to formal data calls. Support proposal reviews and customer presentations as needed.

 - Establish and maintain traceable assumptions, source data, rationale, sensitivities, risks, and cross-functional approvals behind manufacturing estimates and commitments.

 - Assess manufacturing maturity and readiness from concept development through prototype, pilot, low-rate initial production, and full-rate production; identify long-lead investments and enabling decisions early.

 - Develop reusable planning models, benchmarks, proposal content, and industrial reference architectures that improve speed and consistency across future programs.

 - Support broader manufacturing strategy, including network footprint, supplier capacity, facility and capital roadmaps, production technology, and multi-program resource planning.

 - Transition awarded work into execution by converting proposal commitments and assumptions into an initial manufacturing program baseline, readiness plan, and clear ownership across the operating teams.

Required Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, aerospace, industrial, manufacturing, or systems engineering, or a related technical field.

 - 8 or more years of relevant experience in aerospace or defense manufacturing, industrialization, operations strategy, advanced program planning, or technical proposal development.

 - Demonstrated ability to turn early, incomplete technical and program inputs into a structured manufacturing plan with explicit assumptions, risks, and decision points.

 - Experience developing bottom-up manufacturing cost, labor, capacity, tooling, equipment, facility, or production ramp estimates and documenting the basis of estimate.

 - Working knowledge of aircraft production, new product introduction, manufacturing process selection, supply chain strategy, production test, and prototype-to-rate transition.

 - Strong analytical skills and proficiency building clear, auditable models in Excel or comparable tools.

 - Ability to synthesize complex cross-functional inputs into concise written proposals, executive recommendations, and customer-facing presentations.

 - Ability to work independently, make sound decisions with imperfect information, and deliver high-quality work under accelerated proposal timelines.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Master’s degree in engineering, industrial systems, operations management, business, or a related field.

 - Experience supporting defense captures, requests for information, requests for proposals, proposal color-team reviews, or government cost and pricing submissions.

 - Experience developing manufacturing strategies for aircraft, autonomous systems, or other complex electromechanical products.

 - Familiarity with government proposal requirements, basis-of-estimate development, cost estimating relationships, and manufacturing risk and opportunity analysis.

 - Experience with industrial engineering methods such as line balancing, capacity analysis, factory layout, discrete-event simulation, or production system modeling.

 - Experience planning greenfield or brownfield production facilities, capital equipment portfolios, supplier capacity, or production surge strategies.

 - Hands-on experience taking a hardware program from prototype builds into low-rate or full-rate production.

Description:

**THE COMPANY**

For over 40 years, Aero Simulation, Inc. (ASI) has provided quality flight training devices to the US Military. ASI has successfully built numerous training systems with a primary focus on aircrew and maintenance training systems. Our current programs include, but are not limited to, the B-1 Training Systems (Air Force), E-2D Training Systems (Navy), CH-53E Training Devices (USMC), IMOMS (Coast Guard), Navigation, Seamanship, Shiphandling Trainer – NSST (Navy). To learn more about ASI visit Programs- Aero Simulation, Inc.

ASI is a 100% employee-owned engineering and manufacturing company committed to supporting the nation’s warfighters. Being 100% employee-owned directly impacts our culture: it drives our decision-making, motivates our teams, increases our productivity, improves retention and contributes to the future success of our company. Our culture is one where we work hard for our clients and for each other – and we have fun collaborating, sharing experience and expertise, and learning along the way. We strive to deliver exceptional quality, elevate client relationships, and enrich the careers and lives of our employee-owners. As Employee-Owners, we are invested in the success and continued development of each other and the company.

In addition to the Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), we offer a flexible work environment, generous paid time off, professional development opportunities, industry competitive compensation, and superior benefits to include medical, dental, 401k and more!

ASI is a great place to build a career and grow with a company that is dedicated to quality, service and to fostering a community of support for each and every member of the team. To learn more about this opportunity, keep reading!

**POSITION SUMMARY**

ASI is seeking an experienced, results-driven Director of Production to provide strategic leadership and operational oversight of its production organization. This is a key senior leadership position responsible for ensuring the successful manufacturing, assembly, integration, and delivery of ASI's advanced simulation and military training device hardware.

Based in Tampa, Florida, and reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer (COO), the Director of Production will oversee Production Control, Material Control, and Manufacturing through functional managers and department leads. The position will also provide executive oversight of Facility Management and Workplace Safety through the Facilities Manager.

The successful candidate will bring demonstrated experience leading complex manufacturing operations, developing high-performing teams, managing production capacity and resources, and delivering technical products in demanding, schedule-driven environments.

This individual will play an important role in supporting ASI's Department of Defense, U.S. military, government agency, and defense industry programs while ensuring the organization is positioned to support new business opportunities and long-term growth.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

*Strategic Leadership & Operational Management*

* Provide strategic direction and operational leadership for Production Control, Material Control, and Manufacturing.
* Establish production priorities, performance expectations, resource requirements, and organizational objectives.
* Lead through functional managers, promoting accountability, operational discipline, and effective execution.
* Ensure production operations consistently meet contractual commitments, customer requirements, program milestones, and delivery schedules.
* Partner with executive leadership to develop operational strategies supporting current programs and future business growth.
* Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure organizational effectiveness and drive improvement.

*Production Planning & Program Execution*

* Oversee production planning, scheduling, capacity management, and resource allocation across multiple concurrent programs.
* Partner with Program Management and Engineering to translate contractual requirements and technical specifications into executable production plans.
* Ensure production readiness, including personnel, materials, equipment, facilities, documentation, and approved manufacturing processes.
* Identify and mitigate production risks that could impact cost, schedule, quality, or customer delivery.
* Support program reviews, production readiness assessments, customer meetings, and government inspections.
* Provide production estimates, labor forecasts, capacity assessments, and schedule inputs for new business proposals.

*Manufacturing & Systems Integration*

* Oversee the manufacturing and assembly of complex simulation and training device hardware.
* Ensure effective collaboration between Production and Engineering to promote manufacturability, reliability, and cost-effective designs.
* Support the integration of major simulation hardware components, including visual display systems, motion platforms, and associated subsystems.
* Ensure manufacturing activities follow approved engineering drawings, Bills of Materials (BOMs), configuration requirements, and engineering change processes.
* Drive improvements in production flow, manufacturing efficiency, product quality, and delivery performance.

*Workforce Leadership & Development*

* Lead, mentor, and develop production managers, supervisors, manufacturing engineers, technicians, assemblers, and integration personnel.
* Establish clear performance expectations and accountability standards for functional managers.
* Develop staffing and workforce plans to support current and anticipated production requirements.
* Identify workforce development needs and implement appropriate training and cross-training initiatives.
* Build organizational depth through succession planning, leadership development, and employee engagement.
* Foster a culture centered on safety, quality, teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.

*Materials Management & Supply Chain Coordination*

* Ensure effective coordination between Production and Procurement to maintain material availability and support production schedules.
* Monitor material shortages, supplier performance, inventory levels, and long-lead procurement requirements.
* Establish appropriate material priorities based on program schedules and contractual commitments.
* Ensure effective inventory management, material traceability, and control of customer-furnished and government-furnished property.
* Promote accurate material tracking and accountability through ASI's ERP system.

*Quality & Regulatory Compliance*

* Ensure production operations comply with ASI's ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management System and applicable contractual, customer, government, and regulatory requirements.
* Partner with Quality Assurance to address nonconformances, corrective actions, root-cause analysis, and process improvements.
* Maintain effective production documentation, inspection records, test results, and configuration records.
* Support government quality audits, customer surveillance activities, and acceptance inspections.
* Promote a culture of quality and adherence to approved manufacturing processes throughout the production organization.

*Budget, Cost Control & Performance*

* Develop and manage production budgets, labor forecasts, and operational resource plans.
* Monitor production costs, labor utilization, productivity, rework, and overhead.
* Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing efficiency, reduce waste, and increase production throughput.
* Evaluate production capacity and capital equipment requirements.
* Provide regular operational and financial performance reporting to the COO and executive leadership.
* Support long-term resource planning and investment strategies aligned with anticipated business growth.

*Facility Management & Workplace Safety*

* Provide executive oversight of Facility Management and Workplace Safety through the Facilities Manager.
* Establish strategic priorities for facility readiness, infrastructure reliability, maintenance, and workplace safety.
* Ensure facilities, equipment, and infrastructure adequately support current production requirements and future growth.
* Review facility performance, safety metrics, significant incidents, and corrective actions.
* Coordinate facility investment, capital requirements, and infrastructure planning with the Facilities Manager and COO.
* Promote a safe, organized, and efficient working environment.

*Continuous Improvement*

* Implement Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, 5S, and other operational excellence methodologies, as appropriate.
* Establish consistent production management practices, standard operating procedures, and performance measures.
* Identify opportunities to reduce cycle times, eliminate waste, improve first-pass yield, and increase productivity.
* Drive corrective and preventive actions to resolve recurring operational issues.
* Promote employee engagement, proactive problem-solving, and continuous

**LEADERSHIP EXPECTATIONS**

* Provides leadership and direct supervision of Group Leaders responsible for Manufacturing, Facility Management, Production Control, Workplace Safety, and Stockroom operations, establishing priorities, expectations, and accountability for operational performance, quality, efficiency, safety, and on-time delivery.
* The Director maintains oversight of these functional areas while ensuring alignment with program requirements and organizational objectives. Ensures teams have the resources, processes, equipment, capabilities, and organizational support necessary to maintain safe and efficient operations, support successful program execution, and meet production schedules and contractual commitments.

Requirements:

**EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS**

* 10–15 years of progressive experience in manufacturing, production, or operations management.
* At least 5 years of leadership experience managing production teams, functional managers, and complex manufacturing operations.
* Proven experience overseeing the manufacturing, assembly, integration, and delivery of complex technical products.
* Demonstrated ability to manage production schedules, labor resources, materials, budgets, capacity, and contractual delivery commitments.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production planning, quality management systems, and operational performance metrics.
* Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and drive accountability across multiple functional organizations.
* Excellent leadership, communication, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
* Working knowledge of facility operations, infrastructure, and workplace safety requirements.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, flight simulation, military training systems, or related industries.
* Experience supporting U.S. Department of Defense programs, military customers, or defense prime contractors.
* Experience with complex electromechanical systems and hardware/software integration.
* Familiarity with ISO 9001, Lean Manufacturing, and Six Sigma principles.
* Experience with ERP/MRP systems, production planning tools, and manufacturing performance reporting.
* Familiarity with government contracting, DoD Manufacturing Planning (MIL-HDBK-896), configuration management, and Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT).
* Experience managing multiple concurrent production programs.
* Experience providing executive oversight of facility management, infrastructure planning, capital equipment, and workplace safety functions.

*Technical and Leadership Competencies*

* Defense manufacturing and production operations.
* Mechanical and electrical assembly and integration.
* Simulation hardware manufacturing and testing.
* Production planning, scheduling, and capacity management.
* Configuration management and engineering change control.
* Quality management systems and regulatory compliance.
* Government contracting and DoD acquisition environments.
* ERP/MRP systems and material requirements planning.
* Cost accounting, labor forecasting, and operational performance metrics.
* Strategic thinking and organizational leadership.
* Cross-functional collaboration and resource allocation.
* Leadership development, team building, and change management.
* Accountability for cost, schedule, quality, and delivery performance.

* Delivering production commitments on time and within established cost and quality objectives.
* Building a strong, accountable, and effective production leadership team.
* Maintaining production readiness and sufficient capacity to support current and future programs.
* Improving manufacturing efficiency, productivity, and operational performance.
* Ensuring effective coordination among Production, Engineering, Program Management, Quality, Procurement, and Facilities.

card.description:
About PopUp Bagels

PopUp Bagels is not just a bagel company—we’re a cultural movement. Our stores are small, our vibes are loud, and our energy is contagious. From signature neon and iconic bullhorns to our “Not Famous but Known” mirror, we’ve reimagined not just how a bagel is created, but how it’s enjoyed: Grip, Rip and Dip! With a cult-like following, massive social presence, and unparalleled collaborations with top companies, partners and Brand Ambassadors PopUp Bagels is defining a new food lifestyle brand.

We keep things simple, but we do them really, really well. And our customers agree.

The Role

We're looking for a Regional Director to lead operations at our Nevada cream cheese production facility. This facility will play an important role in supporting PopUp's continued growth and our ability to deliver the products our customers love.

This is a senior operational leadership role responsible for overseeing the day-to-day performance of the facility, from the moment raw materials come through the door to the second finished goods ship out to shops around the country.

Here's what makes this role different from other operations roles: we're building something big, and we're building quickly. With established production facilities and operating procedures already in place, the right person for this role will know how to take proven processes, put them into practice, and continue improving them as we grow.

We're looking for a problem-solver who isn't afraid to roll up their sleeves and find solutions, a leader who earns trust on the floor just as easily as they collaborate with senior leadership, and someone who can translate operational expectations into consistent, measurable results.

This role serves as a key connection between the Nevada production facility and our broader operations leadership team. You'll have the opportunity to influence how we operate, develop our people, and contribute to the continued evolution of our production processes as PopUp expands.

If you're a driven leader who thrives in fast-moving environments, values collaboration, and takes pride in building strong teams and efficient operations, this could be the role for you.

What You'll Do:

Run the Facility. You'll provide day-to-day operational leadership and oversight across Cream Cheese and Schmear production, Warehouse, Quality Assurance, Sanitation, and Equipment Maintenance Working closely with the President of Operations and other facility leaders, you'll implement and maintain established SOPs, manage production schedules, drive throughput targets, and identify opportunities to continuously improve how we operate. You'll be responsible for addressing operational challenges, escalating significant issues when appropriate, and ensuring the facility consistently meets established performance, quality, and safety expectations.

Lead People Who Make an Impact. Building a strong team culture is at the core of this role. You'll recruit, develop, and retain a workforce that makes a genuine impact at PopUp Bagels. You'll coach and support your management team, reinforce established training programs, and identify opportunities to strengthen employee development as the operation grows. You'll create an environment where accountability and recognition go hand in hand. Our hourly workforce is the backbone of this operation, and how you show up for them defines everything.

Manage the Numbers. You'll be accountable for facility-level operational performance, including production costs, labor efficiency, waste reduction, and budget adherence. You'll partner closely with the President of Operations, Finance, and Accounting on budgeting, forecasting, and period-end reporting, and regularly communicate facility performance, challenges, and opportunities to senior leadership. You'll identify ways to improve efficiency and control costs without compromising quality, safety, or people, while supporting broader capital planning and investment decisions.

Drive Supply Chain Alignment. Work directly with our VP of Supply Chain to align production schedules with material availability. You'll oversee raw material procurement planning, inventory controls, and warehouse operations, ensuring established FIFO and food safety standards are consistently followed. You'll collaborate with Supply Chain and other production facilities to support inventory accuracy, product availability, and efficient distribution.

Lead Food Safety & Regulatory Compliance. Champion a food-safety-first culture across every part of the facility. You'll ensure consistent execution of established food safety programs and compliance with applicable FDA regulations, FSMA requirements, HACCP plans, and third-party audit standards (SQF, BRC), as applicable. You'll partner with Quality Assurance and the President of Operations to maintain rigorous in-process and finished product quality standards, address compliance concerns, and implement corrective actions when something doesn't meet the bar.

Collaborate Across the Company. You'll represent Nevada facility operations in company-wide leadership meetings and collaborate with Distribution & Logistics, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and corporate leadership. You'll translate what's happening on the floor into meaningful operational insights, communicate opportunities for improvement, and ensure company priorities and decisions are effectively implemented at the facility level.

Who You Are and What You Bring

We're looking for a leader who is genuinely:

A scrappy problem-solver. When something breaks at 7am or a key ingredient is backordered, you find a way. You're resourceful, calm under pressure, and put in the time to figure it out. You know when to make decisions, when to collaborate, and when to escalate an issue.

A trust-builder. Your team respects you because you've worked to build trust, not because of your title. You're on the floor, you know people's names, and you follow through on what you say.

A galvanizing leader. You provide clear direction, get buy-in, and bring your team along with energy and conviction. People want to work hard for you because they know you'll do the same for them.

Equally at home in a leadership meeting and a production room. You can review financial and operational performance in the morning and troubleshoot a production issue in the afternoon. You don't ask your team to do what you're not willing to do yourself.

Built for growth and continuous improvement. PopUp is growing fast, and our processes will continue to evolve. You appreciate the value of established systems and standards, but you're also comfortable identifying opportunities to make them better. You know how to balance consistency with adaptability as the business scales.

You bring:

* Bachelor's degree in Food Science, Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience. Master's degree (MBA or MS) preferred.
* 8–10+ years of progressive plant or manufacturing operations leadership experience, including demonstrated responsibility for facility performance, team leadership, and operational budgets.
* Experience leading operations in fast-paced manufacturing environments, preferably within growing or multi-site organizations.
* Proven track record of leading high-performing, cross-functional manufacturing teams.
* Prior food and beverage industry experience strongly preferred; dairy, cream cheese, spreads, or related refrigerated food production experience is a significant plus.
* Familiarity with food safety regulatory frameworks, including FSMA, HACCP, GMP, and third-party audit standards (SQF, BRC, AIB).
* Strong financial acumen, including budget management, cost analysis, labor efficiency, and operational performance reporting.
* Working knowledge of production cost drivers, manufacturing KPIs, and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Production Excellence, or equivalent).
* Demonstrated experience implementing and maintaining standardized operating procedures, production processes, and operational controls.
* Experience partnering with corporate Finance, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and Distribution teams.
* Availability and willingness to be on-call on weekends and off-hours to respond to facility disruptions or emergencies.
* Experience supporting capital improvement projects and operational efficiency initiatives.
* A history of building positive, rewarding workplace cultures for hourly workforces.

Physical Requirements

The following physical requirements are representative of those needed to perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made for individuals with qualifying disabilities.

* Ability to walk, stand, and move throughout a production facility for extended periods during daily floor presence and inspections.
* Must be able to work in a manufacturing environment with varying temperatures, including refrigerated dairy production and storage areas, moderate to loud noise levels, and exposure to dairy ingredients and food-grade cleaning agents.
* Occasional lifting of up to 50 pounds may be required.
* Must be able to wear required PPE, including hair nets, beard nets, gloves, and safety footwear when on the production floor.
* Ability to use standard office equipment (computer, monitor, phone, conferencing technology) for extended periods.
* Occasional travel to corporate offices, other production facilities, or external meetings (estimated up to 30%).

PopUp Bagels is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

We do not discriminate based on race, age, ancestry, creed, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, pregnancy, childbirth or related condition, unemployment status, gender identity or expression, transgender status, marital status, domestic violence or sexual violence victim status, national origin, citizenship, disability, covered veteran and/or military status, genetic information, familial status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, and local law. PopUp Bagels conducts pre-employment screenings in compliance with local, state, and federal laws, and utilizes E-Verify to confirm U.S. employment eligibility.

The duties of this position may change from time to time. PopUp Bagels reserves the right to add or delete duties and responsibilities at its discretion. This posting describes the general nature and level of work expected and is not intended to be all-inclusive.

· Plan and direct daily production schedules to meet customer orders, yield targets, and delivery deadlines.

· Oversee receiving, washing, peeling, slicing, dehydration, cooling, packaging, and warehousing processes.

· Monitor dehydration time, temperature, and moisture levels to ensure consistent product texture and shelf stability.

· Track and improve key metrics such as yield, throughput, downtime, waste, and labor efficiency.

· Coordinate with farm operations and procurement on sweet potato supply, storage, and seasonal planning.

**Quality and Food Safety**

· Maintain compliance with FDA requirements, including FSMA and Current Good Manufacturing Practices for animal food, and with AAFCO and applicable state regulations.

· Lead the food safety plan, HACCP or preventive controls program, sanitation procedures, and allergen and pathogen controls.

· Prepare the plant for customer, third-party, and regulatory audits and close out corrective actions promptly.

· Manage lot tracking, traceability, and recall readiness.

People and Safety

· Recruit, train, schedule, coach, and supervise production, sanitation, maintenance, and warehouse staff.

· Promote a strong safety culture and ensure OSHA compliance, including lockout/tagout, machine guarding, and forklift safety.

· Hold team members accountable to standards while building a respectful, engaged workforce.

**Equipment, Facilities, and Budget**

· Oversee preventive maintenance and repairs for dehydrators, slicers, conveyors, packaging lines, and utilities.

· Develop and manage the plant budget, labor plan, and capital requests.

· Manage inventory of raw materials, packaging, and finished goods.

· Lead continuous improvement and lean initiatives to lower cost and increase capacity.

· Demonstrated success managing production teams, budgets, and quality systems.

· Strong communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills.

· Proficiency with Microsoft Office and production or inventory systems.

· Production environment with exposure to heat, moisture, noise, and cold storage areas.

· Ability to stand and walk for extended periods and lift up to 50 pounds.

· Must wear required PPE and follow all plant hygiene rules.

Compensation will be competitive and based on experience.

Pay: From $70,000.00 per year

* Vision insurance

card.description:
Job ID: 530934
 
 
Ash Grove is a CRH company with a legacy dating back to 1882. We combine technical expertise, safety and customer-focused solutions to deliver reliable performance for our customers. We manufacture and supply high-performance, advanced cementitious materials for the most demanding construction and infrastructure needs. With more than 2,000 people across 60 locations in the United States and Canada, we support a wide range of applications, from major infrastructure projects to the development and refurbishment of residential and non-residential buildings that support everyday life, from highways and bridges to schools and commercial buildings.
 
 
To learn more about us go to www.ashgrove.com
 
 
**Job Summary**
The Plant Manager plans, coordinates, and supervises the production operations, hazardous waste fuel program, maintenance activities, quality and safety programs, and other related functions involved in plant operations. This position incorporates directives provided by corporate management into policies and procedures to maintain standards and schedules. The position exercises direct or indirect supervision over a large number of employees.
 
 
**Job Location**

* This role will work out of our plant in Midlothian, TX.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Promote and follow all plant safety guidelines.
* Conducts meetings with plant staff personnel to communicate, coordinate and discuss plant operations.
* Monitors, inspects, and reviews all plant activities.
* Ensures production schedule corresponds with sales forecasts.
* Assists in investigating customer and quality problems and concerns.
* Meets with government agencies and community groups concerning plant activities to ensure compliance with environmental regulations, policies, and standards.
* Prepares regular reports regarding plant production operations.
* Attends Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) training for waste-derived fuel activities.
* Promotes effective job performance through motivation, goals, and providing feedback.
* Promotes the safety program, compliance with safety standards, and participates in safety meetings.
* Establishes plant standards, short-term goals, and long-term strategic plans for production, maintenance, and improvements.
* Discusses new products, equipment, and ideas with staff and vendors.
* Analyzes plant costs and explore methods to improve productivity cost-effectively.
* Uses technology to develop a continuous improvement plan for the plant.
* Troubleshoots various problems and performance barriers.

**Job Requirements**

* Ability to read, write, and understand warning labels, instructions, signs, etc.
* Minimum 4 Year - Bachelors Degree in engineering, chemistry, natural sciences, business administration, or closely related field.
* Professional Engineer (PE) preferred
* Ability to develop and deliver effective presentations
* Ability to make decisions and solve problems with high attention to detail and accuracy
* Ability to make sound independent judgments regularly
* Ability to effectively coach and deliver constructive feedback
* Ability to inspire and develop staff
* Proficient in effective negotiation skills in business and construction contracts
* Proficient in Microsoft Office365
* Ability to effectively use computers for general word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, e-mail, internet, and customized company programs.
* Ability to communicate the company's vision into actionable goals and contributions for plant personnel.
* Ability to network with industry professionals, consultants, vendors, suppliers, regulators, and the community.
* Knowledge of safety and environmental health regulations.
* Knowledge of cement chemistry, physical testing, and concrete performance.
* Knowledge of various systems for cement manufacturing (crushing, grinding, pyro processing, chemistry).
* Ability to work from general policies and procedures.
* Ability to refer to supervisor when clarification or interpretation of the organizational policy

**What CRH Offers You**

* Highly competitive base pay
* Comprehensive medical, dental and disability benefits programs
* Group retirement savings program
* Health and wellness programs
* An inclusive culture that values opportunity for growth, development, and internal promotion

**About CRH**
CRH has a long and proud heritage. We are a collection of hundreds of family businesses, regional companies and large enterprises that together form the CRH family. CRH operates in a decentralized, diversified structure that allows you to work in a small company environment while having the career opportunities of a large international organization.
 
 
If you’re up for a rewarding challenge, we invite you to take the first step and apply today! Once you click apply now, you will be brought to our official employment application. Please complete your online profile and it will be sent to the hiring manager. Our system allows you to view and track your status 24 hours a day. Thank you for your interest!
 
 
Ash Grove Cement, a CRH Company, is an Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Employer.
 
 
EOE/Vet/Disability
 
 
CRH is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, status as a protected veteran or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, or local law.
 
 
AI tools may be used in certain stages of the employment lifecycle, such as candidate review; however, all final employment decisions will be made by a person.
